# Review: Emergency Power Sequence, G-1/G-2, ATS-L/C/E

**Verdict: not ready for FAT.** The sequence as written cannot meet its own 10-second transfer requirement. It also contains two engine shutdowns that would disable the emergency source when it is needed, has no timeouts or failure responses, and states two requirements ("as required", "immediately") that cannot be tested. Below are the findings, a provisional setpoint list, and a corrected replacement for sections 3.1–3.5.

Code references are to NFPA 99, NFPA 110 (Level 1, Type 10), and NEC Article 517/700 by topic. Confirm section numbers against the editions your AHJ has adopted.

## 1. Findings

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-01 | 3.1 vs 3.2 | **Timing is impossible.** 3.2 adds the 3 s confirm delay, engine start, first-generator closure, a 5 s stabilization delay, and synchronization of the second generator before any ATS transfers. The 3 s delay and the 5 s delay alone use 8 of the 10 s, which leaves 2 s to start a 1500 kW diesel. Life safety and critical branch cannot be energized within the Type 10 limit. | Transfer ATS-L and ATS-C as soon as the first generator closes to the dead bus. Move synchronization of the second generator and the ATS-E transfer after that. See FR-EPS-004 to -007. |
| F-02 | 3.2 | Simultaneous transfer of all three ATSs puts the whole hospital emergency load on the bus in one block step. This risks a frequency collapse and a reverse-power trip. NFPA 99/NEC 517 permit delayed automatic connection of the equipment branch. | Stage the transfers: ATS-L and ATS-C first, then ATS-E after a delay and only on a capacity permissive. Subdivide ATS-E loads if the load study requires it. |
| F-03 | 3.1 vs 3.2 | 3.1 says the generators start "immediately". 3.2 says they start after a 3 s confirmation. These statements contradict each other. | One statement: start on loss of normal at any ATS after the delay in SP-01. |
| F-04 | 3.1, 3.2 | The PLC is a single point of failure for life safety. NFPA 110 expects the start signal to come from the transfer switch. | Hardwire the engine-start contacts of each ATS to both generator controllers in parallel with the PLC. ATS-L and ATS-C transfer on their own controllers when the emergency source is available. The PLC only manages synchronization, load-add, and load-shed. |
| F-05 | 3.2 | "Utility loss" is not defined. The document does not say which device senses it, which phases, or what voltage/frequency thresholds apply. | Each ATS senses its own normal source on all phases against SP-03/SP-04. Loss at any ATS starts the generators. |
| F-06 | 3.2 | "Rated voltage and frequency" has no tolerance band, so the step cannot be tested. | Use the generator-ready band in SP-05. |
| F-07 | 3.2 | Dead-bus closure race. If both generators reach the ready band at the same time, both can close onto a dead bus out of phase. | Add hardwired dead-bus arbitration so that only one breaker can close on a dead bus. The second breaker closes only through a sync-check (ANSI 25) permissive. |
| F-08 | 3.2 | No timeouts and no failure responses. The document does not cover fail to start, fail to close, fail to synchronize, or an ATS that fails to transfer. | Use the step table in §3.3 below, which gives every step a timeout and a failure response. |
| F-09 | 3.2 | The synchronizing permissive is not defined. | Use the sync-check window SP-07 and the timeout SP-08. |
| F-10 | 3.3 | "Sheds load as required" cannot be tested. "Available" is not defined. The document does not say what is shed, in what order, on what trigger, or how load is restored. The case where one generator trips while both are carrying load is missing. | Use the load priority table and the shed triggers in §3.4. ATS-L is never shed. Shed on bus overload or underfrequency. Restore in stages when two generators are on the bus. |
| F-11 | 3.4 | **"Retransfer immediately" is unsafe and does not comply.** Utility power often bounces after restoration. NFPA 110 requires an adjustable time delay on retransfer to normal and an unloaded cooldown before engine stop. | Add a retransfer delay (SP-11) and stagger the retransfers (SP-12). Bypass the delay if the emergency source fails. Run unloaded for a cooldown period (SP-13) before stop. |
| F-12 | 3.4 | The retransfer transition type is not stated. An open transition between two live sources can damage motors. Closed transition needs utility approval. | Open item OI-03: choose in-phase monitor, delayed-transition, or closed-transition retransfer per ATS. |
| F-13 | 3.4 | The generator stop is undefined. The document does not say whether the generator breakers open before or after the stop, or what state the generators return to. | Open the breakers after cooldown, stop the engines, and return to Standby (Auto). |
| F-14 | 3.5 | **Low coolant temperature as a shutdown is hazardous.** A cold engine with a failed block heater would be blocked from starting or would trip during an outage. | Make it an alarm only (jacket water heater failure). It must not shut down or inhibit start. |
| F-15 | 3.5 | **Low fuel level as a shutdown is hazardous.** NFPA 110 Level 1 makes low fuel an alarm, not a shutdown. Stopping with fuel still in the tank removes the emergency source early. | Make it an alarm only, with a pre-alarm for refuelling. The engine runs until fuel starvation. |
| F-16 | 3.5 | Required Level 1 shutdowns are missing: overcrank, overspeed, and low lube oil pressure. Emergency stop (local and remote) is also missing. | Add these to the cause-and-effect rows in §3.5. |
| F-17 | 3.5 | The document does not say whether shutdowns are latched, how they reset, or what happens on the bus after a generator trips. | Latched. Local reset at the engine controller after inspection. A trip opens that generator's breaker and the PLC goes to single-generator mode (F-10). |
| F-18 | 3.5 | Engine protection belongs to the engine controller. Generator electrical protection belongs to the protection coordination study. The narrative mixes these with PLC logic. | Reference the engine controller and the coordination study. List only the effects on the sequence. |
| F-19 | Whole | There are no ISA-106 states, no requirement IDs, and no test methods. | Use the state table in §3.2 and the FR-EPS IDs. |
| F-20 | Whole | Abnormal handling is missing: PLC failure, loss of PLC power and restart, communication loss to the generator controllers or ATSs, failed sensing (blown PT fuse), loss of DC control power, and ATS fail position. | See §3.6. |
| F-21 | Whole | Test mode is missing. NFPA 110 requires monthly testing under load and an annual test. The document does not cover a utility failure during a test. | Add a Test state (§3.2) and FR-EPS-030/031. |
| F-22 | Whole | The "generator not in Auto" condition and the remote annunciator required by NFPA 110 are missing. | Add both to the alarms in §3.7. |
| F-23 | Whole | Load basis not given. The document does not show whether one 1500 kW unit carries ATS-L + ATS-C. This decides the whole single-generator strategy. | Open item OI-01: load study. |
| F-24 | 3.1, 3.2 | Numbers appear in prose (3 s, 5 s, 10 s). | Move them to the setpoint list and reference by ID. |

## 2. Setpoint list (provisional)

| ID | Description | Value | Units | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SP-01 | Normal source failure confirm delay (TD-ES) | 3 | s | From input. Confirm: it must fit within SP-02 together with the engine start time. |
| SP-02 | Max time from normal loss to ATS-L/ATS-C on emergency (Type 10) | 10 | s | Code limit |
| SP-03 | Normal source undervoltage dropout / pickup | 85 / 90 | % nominal | Provisional, confirm |
| SP-04 | Normal source frequency band | ±2 | % nominal | Provisional, confirm |
| SP-05 | Generator ready band (voltage / frequency) | ±10 / ±2 | % nominal | Provisional, confirm with vendor |
| SP-06 | Stabilization delay before second-generator sync permitted | 5 | s | From input (moved after ATS-L/C transfer) |
| SP-07 | Sync-check window (slip / phase angle / voltage difference) | 0.1 / 10 / 5 | Hz / deg / % | Provisional, confirm in coordination study |
| SP-08 | Second-generator sync timeout (T-SYNC) | 30 | s | Provisional, confirm |
| SP-09 | Engine overcrank (crank attempts × crank time) | 3 × 15 | s | Provisional, engine controller setting, confirm with vendor |
| SP-10 | Delay before ATS-E transfer after its permissive is met (TD-E) | 5 | s | Provisional, confirm |
| SP-11 | Retransfer to normal delay (TD-RET) | 30 | min | Provisional, confirm with AHJ |
| SP-12 | Stagger between ATS retransfers (TD-STAG) | 5 | s | Provisional, confirm |
| SP-13 | Unloaded cooldown before engine stop (T-COOL) | 5 | min | NFPA 110 minimum, confirm edition |
| SP-14 | Single-generator overload shed threshold / delay | 95 / 2 | % of one-generator kW / s | Provisional, confirm |
| SP-15 | Bus underfrequency fast-shed threshold / delay | 58.5 / 0.5 | Hz / s | Provisional, confirm (60 Hz system) |
| SP-16 | Generator breaker close/open confirm timeout (T-CLOSE) | 1 | s | Provisional, confirm |
| SP-17 | ATS transfer confirm timeout (T-XFER) | 2 | s | Provisional, confirm with ATS vendor |
| SP-18 | Low fuel pre-alarm / low fuel alarm (run time remaining) | TBD | h | Open item OI-05 |

## 3. Corrected replacement for 3.1–3.5

### 3.1 Purpose and boundaries

FR-EPS-001: This module controls the emergency supply from G-1 and G-2 to ATS-L, ATS-C, and ATS-E through the emergency bus. The module starts at the normal-source sensing of each ATS and ends at the load side of each ATS. Engine protection belongs to the G-1/G-2 engine controllers. Electrical protection belongs to the protection coordination study.

Tags used by this module: G-1, G-2, 52-G1, 52-G2, emergency bus voltage/frequency/kW metering, ATS-L, ATS-C, ATS-E (normal/emergency position, source-available, engine-start contacts), and the EPS PLC.

### 3.2 States (SBC)

| State | Entry permissive | Allowed exits | Initiator | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standby (Auto) | Both gens in Auto, no latched shutdown, normal source available at all ATSs | Emergency Start, Test, Manual | Auto / operator | Automatic |
| Emergency Start | Normal loss at any ATS for SP-01 | Emergency Run, Retransfer (normal returns before transfer), Fail | Auto | Automatic |
| Emergency Run – Two Gen | 52-G1 and 52-G2 closed | Emergency Run – One Gen, Retransfer | Auto | Automatic |
| Emergency Run – One Gen | One gen breaker closed, other not closed or tripped | Emergency Run – Two Gen, Retransfer, Fail | Auto | Automatic |
| Retransfer | Normal available at every ATS that is on emergency | Cooldown, Emergency Run (normal fails again) | Auto | Automatic |
| Cooldown | All ATSs on normal | Standby, Emergency Start (normal fails) | Auto | Automatic |
| Test | Operator selects test, normal available | Standby (test end), Emergency Start (normal fails during test) | Operator | Operator-prompted |
| Manual | Operator selects Manual at gen controller | Standby (return to Auto) | Operator | Manual |
| Fail | No gen on bus after start timeout | Emergency Start (operator reset after repair) | Auto | Automatic |

### 3.3 Sequences (SqBC)

**Normal to emergency**

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Monitor normal source at each ATS against SP-03/SP-04 | Loss persists for SP-01 | — | Normal returns within SP-01: stay in Standby. |
| 2 | Start G-1 and G-2 (hardwired ATS contacts and PLC) | Either gen within SP-05 | SP-09 | Gen overcranks: lock it out, alarm. Both overcrank: go to Fail, alarm. |
| 3 | Close first ready gen breaker onto dead bus (arbitrated) | Breaker closed, bus within SP-05 | SP-16 | Lock out that breaker, alarm, close the other gen when ready. |
| 4 | Transfer ATS-L and ATS-C | Both on emergency | SP-17. Total time from loss must not exceed SP-02. | Alarm "ATS fail to transfer". Operator uses bypass-isolation. |
| 5 | Wait SP-06, then synchronize and close second gen | Breaker closed through sync check | SP08 | Stop sync attempt, alarm, go to Emergency Run – One Gen. |
| 6 | Wait SP-10, then transfer ATS-E | ATS-E on emergency | SP-17 | Alarm "ATS fail to transfer". |
| 7 | Hold Emergency Run – Two Gen | — | — | Gen trip: go to Emergency Run – One Gen (§3.4). |

FR-EPS-004: ATS-L and ATS-C are on emergency no later than SP-02 after normal loss. Test: utility-pull test with a recorder at FAT and SAT.
FR-EPS-005: ATS-L and ATS-C transfer without the PLC. Test: disable the PLC and repeat the utility-pull test.
FR-EPS-006: Only one gen breaker can close onto a dead bus. Test: force both gens ready at the same time and confirm one closure.
FR-EPS-007: ATS-E transfers only with both gen breakers closed, or with one gen if the load study (OI-01) permits. Test: block 52-G2 and confirm ATS-E holds.

**Emergency to normal**

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Monitor normal source at each ATS against SP-03/SP-04 | Normal stable for SP-11 | — | Normal fails again: reset timer. Emergency bus fails: bypass the timer and retransfer at once. |
| R2 | Retransfer ATS-E, then ATS-C, then ATS-L, SP-12 apart | All ATSs on normal | SP-17 per ATS | Alarm. That ATS stays on emergency and the gens keep running. |
| R3 | Remove start signal, run unloaded for SP-13 | Cooldown complete | — | Normal fails during cooldown: go to Emergency Start, step 4. |
| R4 | Open gen breakers, stop engines, go to Standby | Both gens stopped and in Auto | SP-16 | Alarm "gen not in Auto". |

FR-EPS-010: No ATS retransfers before SP-11 elapses unless the emergency bus fails. Test: restore utility, measure the retransfer time, then trip the bus during the delay.
FR-EPS-011: The gens run unloaded for SP-13 before stopping. Test: timed observation.

### 3.4 Load priority and shedding

| Priority | Load | Shed rule |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | ATS-L | Never shed |
| P2 | ATS-C | Shed only if P3 shed does not clear the trigger (confirm with OI-01) |
| P3 | ATS-E (sub-blocks per OI-02) | Shed first |

FR-EPS-020: In Emergency Run – One Gen, the PLC sheds P3 when bus kW exceeds SP-14. Test: load bank.
FR-EPS-021: The PLC sheds P3 at once when bus frequency falls below SP-15. Test: trip one gen with both loaded.
FR-EPS-022: The PLC restores shed loads in stages, SP-10 apart, after the second gen closes to the bus. Test: reclose the second gen and observe.

### 3.5 Cause and effect (engine shutdowns and trips)

| Cause | Effect | Latched / auto-reset | Reset method |
|---|---|---|---|
| Overcrank (SP-09) | Stop cranking, lock out gen | Latched | Local reset at engine controller |
| Overspeed | Shut down engine, open gen breaker | Latched | Local reset after inspection |
| Low lube oil pressure | Shut down engine, open gen breaker | Latched | Local reset after inspection |
| High coolant temperature | Shut down engine, open gen breaker | Latched | Local reset after inspection |
| Emergency stop (local or remote) | Shut down engine, open gen breaker | Latched | Release E-stop and reset locally |
| Gen electrical protection (per coordination study) | Open gen breaker | Latched | Local reset at relay |
| Any gen breaker trip in Emergency Run – Two Gen | Go to Emergency Run – One Gen, apply §3.4 | Auto | — |
| Low coolant temperature | Alarm only. No shutdown, no start inhibit. | Auto-reset | — |
| Low fuel level | Alarm only. No shutdown. | Auto-reset | — |

### 3.6 Abnormal handling

| Condition | Response |
|---|---|
| PLC failure (watchdog) | Gens start from the hardwired ATS contacts. ATS-L and ATS-C transfer on their own controllers. ATS-E transfers only through hardwired series contacts of 52-G1 and 52-G2 closed (proposed, OI-04). Alarm. |
| PLC power loss and restart | PLC on DC/UPS supply. On restart, the PLC reads the actual breaker and ATS positions and gives no command until it has the state. |
| Comms loss to gen controllers or ATSs | Start, breaker status, and ATS position are hardwired. Comms carries only monitoring. Alarm. |
| Failed normal sensing (PT fuse) | Treat as normal loss at that ATS. The gens start. |
| Loss of DC control power at a gen | Alarm. Treat that gen as not available. |
| ATS fail position | The mechanically held ATS stays in its last position. |
| Gen breaker fail position | Stays in its last position. Opens on protection trip. |

### 3.7 Alarms and operator interface

Until a rationalized alarm database exists, the module needs these alarms: gen fail to start, gen shutdown (per cause), gen not in Auto, gen breaker fail to close/open, fail to synchronize, ATS fail to transfer/retransfer, load shed active, low fuel pre-alarm and alarm, low coolant temperature, high coolant temperature pre-alarm, low oil pressure pre-alarm, PLC fault, and comms loss. Repeat these on the NFPA 110 remote annunciator.

FR-EPS-030: The operator can start a Test with or without load transfer from the HMI. If normal fails during a Test, the module goes to Emergency Start, step 4. Test: pull utility during a load test.
FR-EPS-031: The HMI shows the state, the breaker and ATS positions, bus kW/V/Hz, the shed status, and the retransfer timer remaining. Test: FAT HMI checklist.

Operations must sign off on states, prompts, and the load priority table before FAT.

### 3.8 Open items

| ID | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| OI-01 | Load study: can one gen carry ATS-L + ATS-C, and the ATS-E step loads | Electrical engineer of record | 2026-11-15 (confirm) |
| OI-02 | ATS-E sub-block list and shed order | Facilities + electrical EOR | 2026-11-15 (confirm) |
| OI-03 | Retransfer type per ATS (in-phase, delayed, or closed transition, with utility approval) | Electrical EOR | 2026-11-30 (confirm) |
| OI-04 | Hardwired ATS-E permissive on PLC failure | Controls lead | 2026-11-30 (confirm) |
| OI-05 | Fuel alarm thresholds and required run time | Facilities + AHJ | 2026-11-30 (confirm) |
| OI-06 | Confirm all "provisional" setpoints and the NFPA 99/110 and NEC editions | Controls lead + AHJ | 2026-12-15 (confirm) |
| OI-07 | Vendor confirmation that the gens reach SP-05 within the SP-02 budget after SP-01 | Gen vendor | 2026-11-15 (confirm) |

**Note on scope:** No SIS (IEC 61511) applies. Engine and electrical protection are referenced to the engine controller and the coordination study, not specified here. The STE pass applies to the replacement text above. The prose in the findings table is review commentary, not narrative text.
